newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli official says Iran has rearmed Hizbollah.
newsitem.headline: Israeli official says Iran has rearmed Hizbollah.

text.p: An Israeli official said on Monday Iran had fully rearmed the Islamic militant Hizbollah in Lebanon since a 17-day Israeli blitz last April depleted the group's arsenal.

The official, who refused to be named, said Iran had made 30 arms shipments in Boeing 747 planes via Damascus over the last nine months to Hizbollah (Party of God) fighters waging a guerrilla war to expel Israeli troops from south Lebanon. Iran denies that it sends arms to Hizbollah.

"Iran is of course very much involved in this effort of improving the capabilities of Hizbollah to face Israel again. Since the Grapes of Wrath operation about 30 special flights (of arms) came from Iran in this context," the official said.

Asked if the arms shipments had restored the group's arsenal to the levels that preceded the Israeli campaign codenamed Grapes of Wrath, he said: "I think it brings them to much more than where they were before."
He could not say what types of weapons were contained in the shipments. Israeli security sources have said Iran supplies Hizbollah with Katyusha rockets, anti-tank missiles and automatic rifles.
Around 1,000 Israeli troops patrol a 15 km (nine-mile) south Lebanon occupation zone carved out by the Jewish state in 1985.
Israel waged a massive land, sea and air assault on Hizbollah in Lebanon last April in what it said was a campaign to halt Katyusha attacks on its northern border.
Nearly 500,000 Lebanese fled their homes during the blitz and at least 200 people, mostly civilians, were killed. Hizbollah fired hundreds of Katyushas at Israel during the fighting.
The official said the arms were transferred from Iranian planes to trucks in Damascus and transported to Hizbollah hideouts in south Lebanon.
He said Syria, which has 35,000 troops in Lebanon, could easily halt the supply: "After the Grapes of Wrath they (Syria) have 100 percent control of Hizbollah."

Israel accuses Syria of encouraging Hizbollah attacks in order to pressure the Jewish state into concessions at the bargaining table. Israel and Syria have failed in more than five years of sporadic peace talks to reach any agreement on the fate of the Golan Heights, occupied by Israel in 1967.
